annotations.title: Could bind him.
annotations.text: vve ſee here that mad men which haue extraordinary ſtrength, are many times poſſeſſed of the diuel: as there iſ alſo a deafe and a dumme diuel, and vncleane ſpirits, which worke theſe effects in men, poſſeſſing their bodies. <mn>◦</mn> Al which things infidels and carnal men folowing only nature and reaſon, attribute to natural cauſes: and the leſſe faith a man hath, the leſſe he beleeueth that the diuel worketh ſuch things.

annotations.title: If I ſhal touch.
annotations.text: [1] So the good Catholike ſaith, If I might but touche one of his Apoſtles, yea one of his Apoſtles napkins, yea but the ſhade of one of his Saincts, I ſhould be better for it. Act. 5. and 19. See S. Chrys. to. 5 cont. Gent. in principio. in vit. Babylæ. Yea S. Baſil ſaith, [2]He that toucheth the bone of a martyr, receiueth in ſome degree holineſſe of the grace or vertue that is therein.

annotations.title: Vertue.
annotations.text: Vertue to heale this womans maladie, proceeded from Chriſt, though ſhe touched but his coate: ſo when the Saincts by their Relikes or garments do miracles, the grace and force thereof commeth from our Sauiour, they being but the meanes or inſtruments of the ſame.

annotations.title: Only beleeue.
annotations.text: [1] It is our common ſpeech, when we require one thing ſpecially, though other things alſo be as neceſſarie, and more neceſſarie. As the Phyſician to his patient, Only haue a good heart: when he muſt alſo keepe a diet, and take potions, things more requiſite. So Chriſt in this great infidelity of the Jews, required only that they would believe he was able to do ſuch a cure, ſuch a miracle, and then he did it: otherwiſe it foloweth in the next Chapter [2], He could not do miracles there becauſe of their incredulity. Againe, for this faith he gaue them here and in all like places health of body, which they deſired, and therefore he ſaith not, Thy faith hath iuſtified thee: but, hath made thee ſafe or vvhole. Againe this vvas the father's faith, vvhich could not iuſtifie the daughter. Whereby it is moſt euident, that this Scripture, and the like, are fooliſhly abuſed of the Heretics to proue that only faith iuſtifieth.

notes.text: Scripture fondly applied to proue onely faith.

annotations.title: Wenche ariſe.
annotations.text: Chriſts miracles, beſides that they be wonders and waies to ſhew his power, be alſo ſignificatiue: as theſe which he corporally raiſed from death, put vs in minde of his raiſing our ſoules from ſinne. <mn>[1]</mn> <mn>[2]</mn> The Scripture maketh ſpecial mention only of three raiſed by our Sauiour. of which three, this wench is one, within the houſe: an other, the widowes ſonne in Naim, now caried out toward the graue: the third, Lazarus hauing been in the graue foure daies, and therfore ſtinking. Which diuerſity of dead bodies, ſignifie diuerſity of dead ſoules, ſome more deſperate then other, ſome paſt al mans hope, and yet by the grace of Chriſt to be reuiued and reclaimed.

notes.text: By three dead, are signified three kind of sinners.
